key_insight: Prediction accuracy alone hides which dimensions of the brain's response space a model actually recovers; the paper introduces target-space recovery profiles that reveal which response dimensions are captured, enabling richer model–brain and brain–brain alignment evaluation.
problem_solved: Current evaluations using aggregate prediction accuracy do not tell which dimensions of the target (brain) response space are recovered, so models can score well while missing important representational axes of neural data.
method: Use repeated fMRI measurements to estimate reliable target response dimensions (noise ceilings and stable subspaces).
Fit predictive models and measure recovery per target dimension (e.g., variance explained / subspace overlap) to build a recovery profile across dimensions.
Compare model–brain and brain–brain recovery profiles to quantify which axes are shared, missed, or unique (unified framework for alignment).
impact: Provides a diagnostic tool that goes beyond aggregate scores to reveal what aspects of neural representations models capture, guiding better model selection, architecture design, and neuroscientific interpretation.
visual_elements: Schematic: neural response space as axes with colored bars showing which dimensions are recovered by a model vs. by repeated brain measurements.
Heatmap: per-dimension variance-explained (recovery profile) for multiple models and brain repeats.
Bar/line plot: cumulative variance recovered vs. number of recovered dimensions (comparison of models).
Brain map inset: cortical areas annotated with summary recovery metrics to link spatial anatomy to recovered dimensions.
paper_title: Beyond Prediction Accuracy: Target-Space Recovery Profiles for Evaluating Model-Brain Alignment
paper_authors: Ken Nakamura, Tomoya Nakai, Ryuto Yashiro, Ayumu Yamashita, Kaoru Amano
